Ramzan Kadyrov: Head of Chechen Republic since 2007.
As France's Minister of Justice, this lawyer and politician abolished capital punishment there in 1981 under President Mitterrand — who is he?
Robert Badinter: French politician, lawyer and author (1928–2024)
Beginning in October 1990, this conflict pitted the government's army against the Patriotic Front, a refugee-founded rebel force led in part by Paul Kagame, and ran until July 1994 — what was it?
Rwandan Civil War: 1990–1994 armed struggle in Rwanda.
Renowned in the Book of Genesis for her hospitality and beauty, this matriarch was the wife of Abraham and mother of Isaac — who is she?
Sarah: Biblical matriarch. Sarah (originally Sarai) is a biblical matriarch, prophet, and major figure in Abrahamic religions.
Pitting Britain and Prussia against France and Austria from 1756 to 1763, this global conflict was later dubbed the 'First World War' by Winston Churchill for its sheer scale — what was it called?
Seven Years' War: Global war among European powers (1756–1763)
Born into a wealthy Caracas family and nicknamed El Libertador, this military officer led six present-day South American nations to independence from Spain — who was he?
Simón Bolívar: Venezuelan statesman and military officer (1783–1830)
After running for president as the 1948 Dixiecrat candidate, this South Carolina senator served 47 years and switched from Democrat to Republican in 1964 — who was he?
A former actor turned anti-establishment politician, this Japanese lawmaker founded a party called Reiwa Shinsengumi and once ran for Tokyo governor — who is he?
Taro Yamamoto: Japanese politician and former actor.
Before becoming the Supreme Court's first African-American justice, he argued 32 civil rights cases before it and won 29 — culminating in the landmark Brown v. Board of Education. Who was he?
Thurgood Marshall: US Supreme Court justice from 1967 to 1991.
Leading Sweden's Moderate Party since 2017, this politician became prime minister in 2022 at the head of a minority coalition and went on to complete his country's accession to NATO. Who is he?
Ulf Kristersson: Prime Minister of Sweden since 2022. Kristersson became party leader after Anna Kinberg Batra resigned in 2017.
Once governor of Donetsk Oblast, this pro-Russian politician served as Ukraine's fourth president until the 2014 Revolution of Dignity drove him into exile in Russia — who is he?
Viktor Yanukovych: President of Ukraine from 2010 to 2014.
What is this — “2021 vehicular mass murder in Wisconsin”?
Waukesha Christmas parade attack: 2021 vehicular mass murder in Wisconsin. The parade was live-streamed, and other attendees captured the incident on videos later posted to social media.
Raging from 1914 to 1918 and nicknamed 'the Great War,' this conflict's mass troop movements helped spread the deadly Spanish flu pandemic — which war?
World War I: 1914–1918 global conflict. The war saw important developments in weaponry including tanks, aircraft, artillery, machine guns, and chemical weapons.

Rooted mostly among rural Indigenous communities in Chiapas, this Mexican far-left group has been in a frozen conflict with the state since 1994 and takes its name from a revolutionary agrarian commander — which group?
Zapatista Army of National Liberation: Far-left political and militant group in southern Mexico.
Which of these four is the eldest?
Patrick Geddes (born 1854) is the earliest of the four.
Which of these people was born first?
Omar Khayyam (born 1048) is the earliest of the four.
Which of these four has been around longest?
C++ (founded 1983) is the earliest of the four.
Which of these four is the oldest?
Haskell (founded 1990) is the earliest of the four.
Which of these four is an astronomer?
Annie S. D. Maunder is an astronomer. As sole author, she also devised with her husband, Edward Walter Maunder, the butterfly diagram for sunspots.
Pick the mathematician from these four.

William James Sidis is a mathematician. Born to Boris Sidis, a prominent psychiatrist, and Sarah Mandelbaum Sidis, a physician, Sidis demonstrated extraordinary intellectual capabilities from infancy.
What is the atomic number of Tellurium?
Tellurium is a chemical element; it has the symbol Te and atomic number 52.
What is the atomic number of Manganese?
Manganese is a chemical element; it has the symbol Mn and atomic number 25.
In what year was David Attenborough born?
David Attenborough: Sir David Frederick Attenborough ( AT-ən-bər-ə; born 8 May 1926) is an English broadcaster, natural historian, and writer.
In what year was Eratosthenes born?
Eratosthenes eventually became the chief librarian at the Library of Alexandria.
In what year was Michael Faraday born?
Michael Faraday: Although Faraday received little formal education, as a self-made man, he was one of the most influential scientists in history.
In what year did Carlo Acutis die?
Carlo Acutis: Acutis was canonised on 7 September 2025, alongside Pier Giorgio Frassati.
In what year did Srinivasa Ramanujan die?
Srinivasa Ramanujan Iyengar (22 December 1887 – 26 April 1920) was an Indian mathematician who worked during the early 20th century.
In what year was Uncertainty principle discovered?
Uncertainty principle: The uncertainty principle, also known as Heisenberg's indeterminacy principle, is a fundamental concept in quantum mechanics.

Mikoyan-Gurevich MiG-21: Russian Aircraft Corporation MiG. Approximately 60 countries across four continents have flown the MiG-21, and it still serves many nations seven decades after its maiden flight.
Zinc: Pfizer. Zinc is a chemical element; it has symbol Zn and atomic number 30.
In which country is Boeing KC-135 Stratotanker?
Boeing KC-135 Stratotanker: United States. It has a narrower fuselage and is shorter than the 707.
Who is credited with discovering Roentgenium?
GSI Helmholtz Centre for Heavy Ion Research
Roentgenium: GSI Helmholtz Centre for Heavy Ion Research. Roentgenium (German: [ʁœntˈɡeːni̯ʊm]) is a synthetic chemical element; it has symbol Rg and atomic number 111.
Who is credited with discovering 4 Vesta?
4 Vesta: Heinrich Wilhelm Olbers. Vesta (minor-planet designation: 4 Vesta) is one of the largest objects in the asteroid belt, with a mean diameter of 525 kilometres (326 mi).
Who is credited with discovering Lysosome?
Lysosome: Christian de Duve. A lysosome (/ˈlaɪsəˌsoʊm/) is a membrane-bound organelle that is found in all animal cells (except red blood cells), and rarely in plant cells.
People with this anxiety disorder dread places they feel they can't escape — crowds, queues, public transit — and in severe cases may become unable to leave home at all. What is it?
Agoraphobia is an anxiety disorder characterized by symptoms of anxiety in situations where the person perceives their environment to be unsafe with no way to escape.
Found on every continent but Antarctica and almost always monogamous breeders, which bird family unites ducks, geese, and swans under one scientific name?
Anatidae are the biological family of water birds that includes ducks, geese, and swans.
Native to Europe but introduced to North America, this orb-weaver spider species is known by several common names, one of them shared confusingly with a different species — which species?
Araneus diadematus is commonly called the European garden spider, cross orbweaver, diadem spider, orangie, cross spider, and crowned orb weaver.
Derived from a particular acid, this class of depressant drugs once treated anxiety and insomnia, but their overdose risk got them largely replaced by benzodiazepines and 'Z-drugs' — what are they?
Barbiturate are a class of depressant drugs that are chemically derived from barbituric acid.
This brittle, silvery-white post-transition metal can develop a vividly iridescent, rainbow-colored surface from thin-film oxidation when heated. What element is it?
Bismuth is a chemical element; it has symbol Bi and atomic number 83.
This outdated 19th-century term for what's now called acute or chronic nephritis was marked by swelling and albumin showing up in the urine — what was it called?
Bright's disease is a historical classification of kidney diseases that are described in modern medicine as acute or chronic nephritis.
Bordered by Aquila, Sagittarius, and Aquarius in the sky's watery region, this half-goat, half-fish zodiac figure is the tiniest of the twelve — which constellation?
Capricornus is one of the constellations of the zodiac.
This genus of deciduous trees and shrubs in the beech family, native to the temperate Northern Hemisphere, gives its name to a widely eaten edible nut it produces — what's this tree (and nut) called?
Chestnut are the deciduous trees and shrubs in the genus Castanea, in the beech family Fagaceae.

Native to Australasia and ranging from the Philippines to the Solomon Islands, these 21 parrot species are recognizable by their prominent crests and curved bills, with plumage that's mostly white, grey, or black — name the group?
Cockatoo is any of the 21 species of parrots belonging to the family Cacatuidae, the only family in the superfamily Cacatuoidea, native to Australasia.

This family of fifteen tall, long-necked bird species mostly wears muted gray-and-white plumage with a patch of bare red skin on the face — except for one crowned genus that stands out — what bird is it?
Crane (bird) are a type of large bird with long legs and necks in the biological family Gruidae of the order Gruiformes.
When insulin runs short, the body burns fat into acidic ketones, causing deep gasping breaths and fruity-smelling breath in this potentially life-threatening emergency — what is it?
Diabetic ketoacidosis (DKA) is a potentially life-threatening acute complication of diabetes mellitus.
This social science examines the production, distribution, and consumption of goods and services, analyzing everything from individual agents to entire economies. What discipline is this?
Economics is a social science that studies the production, distribution, and consumption of goods and services.

A German Jew who fled the Nazi regime for the United States, this social psychologist and psychoanalyst co-founded a New York psychiatric institute and was associated with the Frankfurt School of critical theory — who is he?
Erich Fromm (March 23, 1900 - March 18, 1980) was a German-American social psychologist, psychoanalyst, sociologist, humanistic philosopher, and democratic socialist.
This plant genus of roughly 850 species includes woody trees, vines, and epiphytes native to the tropics, though only two species are widely cultivated for their sweet fruit — what genus is it?
Ficus (or) is a genus of about 850 species of woody trees, shrubs, vines, epiphytes and hemiepiphytes in the family Moraceae.

This Austrian engineer founded a firearms company in 1963; when his first pistol entered Austrian service in 1982, its famous model number referred to his 17th patent, not the rounds it held — who is he?
Gaston Glock (19 July 1929 - 27 December 2023) was an Austrian engineer and businessman.

Five species of this group of plants — rice, wheat, maize, barley, and sugar cane — together cover 46 percent of the world's arable land, alongside two related families, sedges and rushes. What kind of plant is this?
Grass refers to various families of plants.
Credited with putting middle-class Americans behind the wheel, this industrialist lent his surname to the very philosophy of assembly-line manufacturing. Who is he?
Henry Ford (July 30, 1863 - April 7, 1947) was an American industrialist and business magnate.
Classified under sleep-wake disorders in the DSM-5, this condition causes a lack of alertness during waking hours despite — or because of — too much sleep. What is it?
Hypersomnia is a neurological disorder of excessive time spent sleeping or excessive sleepiness.
Whose 1687 book Principia Mathematica achieved the first great unification in physics and established classical mechanics?
This Johns Hopkins psychologist coined the terms 'gender role' and 'sexual orientation' and believed gender was malleable during a child's first two years. Who was he?
John Money (8 July 1921 - 7 July 2006) was a New Zealand American psychologist, sexologist and professor at Johns Hopkins University known for his research on human sexual behavior and gender.
This fatal prion disease, once common among the Fore people of Papua New Guinea, was nicknamed 'laughing sickness' and spread through ritual funerary cannibalism. What is it?
Kuru (disease) was a rare, incurable, and fatal neurodegenerative disorder that was formerly common among the Fore people of Papua New Guinea.
One of only five people to win multiple Nobel Prizes, this American chemist and peace activist is the sole person to have received two unshared Nobels — one in Chemistry, one for Peace. Who is he?
Linus Pauling (February 28, 1901 - August 19, 1994) was an American chemist and peace activist.

This colorless, highly water-soluble inorganic salt forms hydrates holding up to 12 water molecules per unit, and its anhydrous form is industry's main source for producing a lightweight, silvery-white structural metal — which compound is it?
Magnesium chloride is an inorganic compound with the formula MgCl2.
This nitrogen-heavy compound forms durable plastic resins used in dry-erase boards and dinnerware, and its foam version scrubs stains as the innards of a Magic Eraser — name the chemical?
Melamine is an organic compound with the formula C3H6N6.

An Egyptian who studied architecture at Cairo University and worked as a civil engineer, this man was the oldest of the 19 hijackers and the ringleader who piloted American Airlines Flight 11 into the North Tower — who was he?
Mohamed Atta (September 1, 1968 - September 11, 2001) was an Egyptian engineer, architect, and the lead terrorist hijacker for al-Qaeda on American Airlines Flight 11.
This stocky Arctic whale carries a spiralled tusk up to three metres long — actually a protruding left canine tooth thought to serve as weapon, tool, and sensor — what is it?
Narwhal (Monodon monoceros) is a species of toothed whale native to the Arctic.
This condition causes involuntary, repetitive eye movements, sometimes present from birth and sometimes acquired later in life, often reducing visual clarity. Name the condition?
Nystagmus is a condition of involuntary (or voluntary, in some cases) eye movement.
This genus of big cats contains the five largest living felines — jaguar, leopard, lion, snow leopard, and tiger — along with extinct relatives like the cave lion — what's the genus called?
Panthera is a genus within the family Felidae, and one of two extant genera in the subfamily Pantherinae.
Fill in the blank: “____ (born 12 January 1971) is a Danish convicted murderer and former entrepreneur.”

Peter Madsen (born 12 January 1971) is a Danish convicted murderer and former entrepreneur. Peter Langkjær Madsen (Danish: [ˈpʰe̝ˀtɐ ˈlɑŋˌkʰeˀɐ̯ ˈmæsn̩]; born 12 January 1971) is a Danish convicted murderer and former entrepreneur.
This genus of single-celled parasites moves from mosquito to human bloodstream, destroying red blood cells and causing a disease with recurring fevers — what is this genus called?
Plasmodium is a genus of unicellular eukaryotes that are obligate parasites of vertebrates and insects.
Used to treat high blood pressure, irregular heart rhythms, performance anxiety and migraine prevention, this beta blocker medication reaches the bloodstream within 30 minutes of dosing — which drug?
Propranolol is a medication of the beta blocker class. It can be taken orally, rectally, or by intravenous injection.
An Indian industrialist and philanthropist who twice led one of the country's biggest business groups, he descended from its founder and trained as an architect at Cornell. Who was he?
Ratan Tata (28 December 1937 - 9 October 2024) was an Indian industrialist and philanthropist.

Originally bred in Germany to herd livestock and pull carts of butchered meat to market until railways took over in the mid-1800s, this medium-to-large mastiff-type dog now also works as a guard and police dog - name the breed?
Rottweiler (UK also) is a breed of domestic mastiff type dog, regarded as medium-to-large or large.
First described in 1779, which large African raptor stands over four feet tall on stilt-like legs and is grouped in its own family, Sagittariidae?
Secretarybird (Sagittarius serpentarius) is a large bird of prey that is endemic to Africa.
Once placed alone in the genus Uncia before phylogenetics moved it into Panthera, this high-altitude cat ranges across the Tibetan Plateau and Himalayas — what is it?
Snow leopard (Panthera uncia) is a species of large cat in the genus Panthera of the family Felidae.

Starting with fever and flu-like symptoms before the skin blisters and peels into painful raw patches, this severe drug-triggered skin reaction sits on the same disease spectrum as toxic epidermal necrolysis, only less severe — which condition?
Stevens–Johnson syndrome (SJS) is a type of severe skin reaction.
Defined as applying conceptual knowledge to reach practical goals in a repeatable way, this field covers both tangible machines and intangible things like software — what is it?
Technology is the application of conceptual knowledge to achieve practical goals, especially in a reproducible way.
A nightshade-family relative of tobacco and the potato, this South American native arrived in Eurasia via the Columbian exchange and is botanically a berry eaten as a vegetable — what is it?
Tomato (Solanum lycopersicum) is a plant whose fruit is an edible berry that is eaten as a vegetable.

Constantly produced by cells lining the lower female reproductive tract, this fluid mixture of liquid, cells, and bacteria varies throughout the menstrual cycle and helps lubricate and protect the area — what is it called?
Vaginal discharge is a mixture of liquid, cells, and bacteria that lubricate and protect the vagina.
This American child prodigy, son of a prominent psychiatrist, lectured on four-dimensional geometry at age 12 and graduated from Harvard cum laude at 16. Who was he?

William James Sidis (April 1, 1898 - July 17, 1944) was an American child prodigy whose exceptional abilities in mathematics and languages made him one of the most famous intellectual prodigies of the early 20th century.

Best known for the Cities of Salt quintet chronicling how oil discovery upended traditional Bedouin life, this novelist's criticism of Middle Eastern elites led Saudi Arabia to revoke his citizenship — who is he?

Originally launched in 2008 as Bombardier's CSeries, this five-abreast narrow-body airliner family was rebranded in 2018 after a European aerospace giant acquired a majority stake. What's it called today?
Airbus A220: Canadian narrow-body airliner family. The Airbus A220 is a family of five-abreast narrow-body airliners by Airbus Canada Limited Partnership (ACLP).
This military pilot became his country's first astronaut when he flew to the International Space Station aboard a 2024 mission — who is he?
Alper Gezeravcı: Turkish fighter pilot and astronaut (born 1979)
A towering 20th-century French mathematician known for foundational work in number theory and algebraic geometry, he was a principal founder of the Bourbaki group. Who was he?

Latin for 'worm-shaped,' this finger-like, blind-ended tube branches off the cecum and, though long considered vestigial, may actually serve as a reservoir for beneficial gut bacteria. What structure is this?
Appendix (anatomy): Tube attached to the intestine.
From the Greek for 'lack of order,' this neurological sign involves loss of voluntary muscle coordination, often linked to cerebellum dysfunction — what is it called?
Ataxia: Neurological impairment of voluntary muscle movement.
Originating in Central Africa, this hunting dog breed doesn't bark but makes an unusual yodel-like sound instead, earning it a nickname — what breed is it?
Basenji: Central African breed of dog. The Fédération Cynologique Internationale places it in the Spitz and "primitive types" categories, while the American Kennel Club classifies it as a hound.
Coined by Károly Ereky in 1919, this multidisciplinary field harnesses bacteria, yeast, and plants — often via genetic engineering — to create products and services. What field?
Biotechnology: Use of living systems and organisms to develop or make useful products.
Also known as the penny bun or porcino, this prized edible fungus can grow a brown cap up to a foot wide and forms symbiotic partnerships with forest tree roots — which mushroom?
Boletus edulis: Species of mushroom, widely distributed in the Northern Hemisphere.
Bred in the 19th century as a guard dog by crossing the English Mastiff with the now-extinct Old English Bulldog, which large, short-muzzled English breed was recognized by the Kennel Club in 1924?
Bullmastiff: English breed of dog. The Bullmastiff is an English breed of dog of mastiff type and large size, with a solid build and a short muzzle.
This Sicilian pastry is a fried, tube-shaped shell filled with sweet ricotta, dressed up with candied orange zest in Palermo or chopped pistachios in Catania — what treat is it?
Cannoli: Italian ricotta-filled pastry. Cannoli are Sicilian pastries consisting of a tube-shaped shell of fried pastry dough, filled with a sweet and creamy filling containing ricotta cheese.
Native to the western Himalayas and the Mediterranean's high altitudes, this coniferous genus bears erect cones and wood that naturally repels moths — which genus?
Found across North America (and one Siberian species in Asia), these small striped squirrels stash food in their cheek pouches to store for winter — what are they?
This spore-forming, rod-shaped bacterium produces the most potent toxin known to science, causing a severe paralytic illness often linked to bulging canned food — what's its name?
Clostridium botulinum: Species of endospore forming bacterium.

This grayish-brown, wart-skinned amphibian (scientific name Bufo bufo) is found across most of Europe, hides by day, and hunts invertebrates at dusk, moving with a slow, ungainly walk or short jumps — which species?
Common toad: Species of amphibian. It belongs to a group of closely related species descended from a common ancestral line of toads and forming a species complex.
Surprisingly, the closest living relatives of birds are a clan of semiaquatic predators that includes alligators, caimans, and the long-snouted gharial. What is this reptile order?
Crocodilia: Order of reptiles. The teeth are conical and peg-like, and the bite is powerful.
This Manhattan Project physicist later led the Federation of American Scientists and is best remembered for his 1959 Senate testimony opposing Lewis Strauss's Commerce nomination — who is he?
David L. Hill: American nuclear physicist (1919–2008)
Named for the unique double-beamed bones under its tail, this long-necked Jurassic giant is one of the most common fossils found in North America's Morrison Formation. What dinosaur is it?
Diplodocus: Genus of diplodocid sauropod dinosaurs (fossil)
Starting life bilaterally symmetrical as larvae but growing into five-pointed radial adults, this animal phylum includes starfish, sea urchins, and sea cucumbers — what is it called?
Echinoderm: Marine phylum of animals often with radial symmetries.

This anaerobic parasite infects tens of millions of people worldwide, causing a gut disease whose name comes from a word meaning tissue disintegration, and kills over 55,000 people each year — what is it?
With a glossy black head and a distinctive white bill shield, this rail-family waterbird is found from Europe to Australia — which bird?
Eurasian coot: Species of bird. The Eurasian coot (Fulica atra), also known as the common coot or Australian coot, is a member of the rail and crake bird family, the Rallidae.
A feathery, yellow-flowered Mediterranean herb in the carrot family, this anise-tasting plant is one of the primary ingredients in absinthe — what is it?
Fennel: Flowering plant species in the carrot family.
Developed by IBM with a reference manual released in 1956, this programming language became the go-to choice for numerical weather prediction and supercomputer benchmarks — what language is it?

Marked by heartburn, regurgitation, and even dental corrosion from stomach acid creeping back up the digestive tract, this chronic condition can, if untreated, lead to esophageal stricture or Barrett's esophagus — what is it?
Gastroesophageal reflux disease: Flow of stomach contents into the esophagus.
Produced by the pancreas's alpha cells, this hormone raises blood sugar by triggering the liver to break down stored glycogen — the functional opposite of insulin. What is it?
Glucagon: Peptide hormone. It raises the concentration of glucose and fatty acids in the bloodstream and is considered to be the main catabolic hormone of the body.
Credited as the inventor of radio, this Italian engineer shared the 1909 Nobel Prize in Physics and later set up Vatican Radio for Pope Pius XI — who is he?
Guglielmo Marconi: Italian radio-frequency engineer and inventor (1874–1937)
Despite common nicknames like 'Christmas rose' and 'Lenten rose,' this poisonous Eurasian flowering genus isn't actually related to roses at all — what is it?
Discovered in 2013 in South Africa's Rising Star Cave system, this small-brained archaic human species yielded over 1,500 bone specimens from at least 15 individuals — which species?
Homo naledi: South African archaic human species. The initial discovery comprises 1,550 specimens of bone, representing 737 different skeletal elements, and at least 15 different individuals.
A person with this condition becomes unduly alarmed by even the most minor symptom, convinced a serious illness is upon them despite no medical diagnosis — what is it?
Hypochondriasis: Excessive fear of developing illness.
This cerebrovascular condition is a localized ballooning of a brain blood vessel most often found in the Circle of Willis, with the 'berry'-shaped type being the most common. What is it?

Intracranial aneurysm: Ballooning or rupturing of a blood vessel in the brain. The risk of rupture varies with the size and location of the aneurysm, with those in the posterior circulation being more prone to rupture.
This Swiss psychologist's theory of cognitive development in children gave rise to a field he called genetic epistemology — who was he?

Also called legal theory, this field applies philosophical methods to questions like what the law is and how it ought to be — with roots traced to Confucius, Aristotle, and Enlightenment thinkers like Locke and Rousseau. What field is it?

Nicknamed 'acid' and 'Lucy' and derived from the ergot fungus, this semisynthetic hallucinogen is so potent that 20 micrograms produces noticeable effects — yet no fatal human overdose has ever been documented — what is it?
Born in Germany, this businessman founded the first company to manufacture blue jeans, beginning operations in San Francisco in 1853 — who is he?
Marketed as Imodium, this opioid-class medication treats diarrhea without crossing the blood-brain barrier at normal doses?
Loperamide: Medicine used to reduce diarrhea.
Males of this widespread dabbling duck species sport iridescent green heads, while females have brown-speckled plumage — which bird?
Mallard: Species of duck. The mallard or wild duck (Anas platyrhynchos) is a dabbling duck that breeds throughout the temperate and subtropical Americas, Eurasia, and North Africa.
Distinguished by its darker camouflage, conformal fuel tanks, and a two-seat cockpit, this all-weather multirole fighter first flew in 1986 for long-range interdiction missions — what is it?
McDonnell Douglas F-15E Strike Eagle: American all-weather multirole fighter aircraft.
First made in 1969 and approved for medical use in 1978, this selective beta blocker treats high blood pressure, angina, and helps prevent migraines — what is it called?
Metoprolol: Beta blocker medication. It is also used to prevent further heart problems after myocardial infarction and to prevent headaches in those with migraines.
Sold under the brand name Provigil, this first-line narcolepsy treatment boosts dopamine without the euphoria or addiction risk of classic stimulants like amphetamine — what is it?
This autoimmune disease attacks acetylcholine receptors at the neuromuscular junction, often causing drooping eyelids, double vision, and difficulty swallowing — which condition?
Myasthenia gravis: Autoimmune disease resulting in skeletal muscle weakness.
This semiaquatic salamander's juvenile phase is nicknamed an 'eft,' and adults return to the water every year to breed after living mostly on land — what is it?
Newt: Salamander in the subfamily Pleurodelinae.
Thriving in the cool, wet summers of Northwest Europe, this hardy cereal grass tolerates low-nutrient, acidic soil and is dominated globally by Canadian and Russian production?
Derived from an ancient Roman unit called the uncia, this measure comes in an avoirdupois version equal to 1/16 of a pound and a heavier troy version used for precious metals — what unit is it?
Ounce: Unit of mass. The ounce is any of several different units of mass, weight, or volume and is derived almost unchanged from the uncia, an Ancient Roman unit of measurement.
Also called androgenetic alopecia, this condition driven by male sex hormones and genetics shows up as a receding hairline or a thinning crown in men — what's the common name for it?
Pattern hair loss: Medical condition. Pattern hair loss, also known as androgenetic alopecia, is a hair loss condition that primarily affects the top and front of the scalp.
This legume's raw seeds contain a toxic compound that must be boiled away before eating, though its unripe green pods are eaten as-is — which species is it?

Derived in 1900 by a German physicist who proposed that an oscillator's energy could only change in discrete increments, this principle describes the spectral density of radiation from a black body at a given temperature — what is it called?
Planck's law: Spectral density of light emitted by a black body.
This common name describes small aquatic crustaceans with an exoskeleton and ten legs, especially popular in the UK and Commonwealth nations for larger swimming decapods — what is it?
Prawn: Common name applied to some types of crustaceans.
Ranging from Penguin Random House to countless small independent players, which broad industry covers making books, magazines, music, and software available to the public, in print or digital form?
Publishing: Production and distribution of media.

The largest of the true foxes and the most widely distributed carnivore on Earth, this Northern Hemisphere native is so destructive where it's been introduced that it made the list of the world's 100 worst invasive species — which animal is it?
Red fox: Species of mammal. The red fox (Vulpes vulpes) is the largest of the true foxes, and the most widely distributed member of the order Carnivora.
The wild ancestor of the domestic pigeon, this pale grey bird has two black bars on each wing and gave rise to feral pigeons worldwide — what is it?
Rock dove: Ancestor of domestic pigeon. The domestic pigeon, often called "Columba livia domestica", which includes about 1,000 different breeds, is descended from this species.

A member of the mint family native to the Mediterranean, this grayish-leaved perennial subshrub is used both in cooking and as an ornamental garden plant — which herb, better known by its common name sage?
Salvia officinalis: Species of plant. Salvia officinalis, common sage or sage, is a perennial, evergreen subshrub, with woody stems, grayish leaves, and blue to purplish flowers.
Broader than linguistics, this field studies how signs — from words to maps to clothing — form systems that carry meaning, split into syntactics, semantics, and pragmatics — what is it called?
Semiotics: Study of signs. It is an interdisciplinary field that examines what signs are, how they form sign systems, and how individuals use them to communicate meaning.
Living in damp spots like rotting wood, these polyphyletic organisms combine into fruiting bodies that release spores to help decompose dead plants — what are they?
A competitive physical activity that maintains or improves physical ability and skills, this can involve teams or individuals and may be open to broad participation or restricted. What is this?
Sport: Forms of competitive activity, usually physical.
Nicknamed the "Super Flanker" and derived from the Su-27, this twin-engine, supermaneuverable Russian air superiority fighter first flew as a prototype in 1988 — what is it?
Sukhoi Su-35: Upgraded series of the Su-27 fighter aircraft.
Nicknamed the brown raptor, this nocturnal bird of prey nests in tree hollows across Europe and is so territorial that evicted youngsters may starve — what is it?
Tawny owl: Stocky medium-sized owl species.
Nicknamed thunderflies, these minute fringe-winged insects are too feeble for normal flight, so they fly using a 'clap and fling' trick that conjures lift from tiny vortices. What are they?
Thrips: Order of insects. Thrips are a functionally diverse group; many of the known species are fungivorous.
Botanically a perennial with an elongated trunk, this form isn't a single family — palms, ferns, and bamboos all independently grew tall stems to win at chasing sunlight. What is it?
Tree: Perennial woody plant with elongated trunk.
Medically called micturition or voiding, this voluntary process happens up to seven times a day in a healthy adult — what is it?
